TasteForge Inc. - Q3 2023 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the TasteForge Inc. Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if using a telephone, or click the Q&A button in the webcast interface if joining online. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss TasteForge Inc.'s Q3 2023 results. Joining me on the call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Growth Officer; and David Ruiz, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson (CEO):
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 2023. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on five key areas: impact of new product innovations and launches, organic sales growth guidance for the next quarter and year, impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions, EPS guidance and key assumptions, and organic revenue growth overall and by region.

First, regarding the impact of new product innovations and launches. These continue to serve as a key growth engine for TasteForge. In Q3, these initiatives generated $285 million in incremental revenue, accounting for 18% of our total net sales growth year-over-year and driving 22% of our overall top-line expansion. This is the third straight quarter where innovations have outperformed our core portfolio, highlighting our dedication to leading categories in the Food & Beverage industry as consumers shift toward health, sustainability, and convenience.

Let me detail this across product categories, financial outcomes, regional variations, and our path forward. Our R&D efforts, supported by a $120 million investment in fiscal 2023—including collaborations with biotech partners like Impossible Foods on protein extrusion technology—resulted in four significant launches this year. At the forefront is our VitaBloom functional beverage line, featuring zero-sugar, adaptogen-infused sparkling water aimed at the $15 billion global functional drinks market, which expanded 12% year-over-year according to Nielsen. VitaBloom posted $95 million in Q3 sales, with distribution velocity rising 45% in the first 90 days across 25,000 U.S. retail outlets, including nationwide availability at Walmart and Kroger. Gross margins reached 52%, 300 basis points above our company average, due to efficient co-packing at our aseptic filling facility in Georgia, where lightweight PET innovations cut packaging costs by 15%.

In the snacks category, our EarthCrunch plant-based protein bars—made with upcycled pea protein and using 20% less water per unit—secured 8% market share in the $6 billion U.S. better-for-you snack segment within just six months. Q3 sales hit $72 million, propelled by 35% of volume coming from e-commerce on platforms like Amazon and Thrive Market. Velocity improved 28%, with repeat purchase rates at 62%, thanks to clean-label features such as no artificial preservatives and certified B-Corp sustainable sourcing. Margins grew to 48% through supply chain improvements, including direct procurement from Brazil's pea harvest areas.

We also introduced PureHarvest keto-ready meal kits in the refrigerated prepared foods section, entering the $10 billion meal kit market growing at a 9% CAGR per Euromonitor. These delivered $58 million in Q3, with trial rates of 24% in test markets such as Target and Whole Foods. Initial data indicates lifetime value per household at 2.8 times acquisition cost, backed by insights from our proprietary TastePanel app surveying 50,000 panelists on low-carb preferences.

Overall, these new products reached break-even in an average of four months, surpassing our six-month goal, enabled by pricing at a 15-20% premium to category averages amid premiumization trends where shoppers pay 22% more for functional attributes, per IRI data. Financially, innovations propelled organic growth to 11%, countering 2% foreign exchange headwinds. Blended gross margins for new items stood at 50.2%, boosting company-wide margins by 110 basis points to 42.5%. SG&A for these products was 18% of sales, below our historical 22%, thanks to digital marketing gains like 30% lower cost-per-click through TikTok Shop and partnerships with influencers akin to those with Celsius Holdings.

We're capitalizing on megatrends: health and wellness drove 45% of new sales from low/no-sugar, high-protein items; sustainability 30% from upcycled and plant-based offerings in line with EU Green Deal requirements; and convenience 25% from ready-to-drink formats. Inventory turns for innovations reached 9.2 times, compared to 7.5 times company-wide, reducing obsolescence in an environment where CPG input costs rose 8% year-over-year per USDA indices.

Regionally, North America, representing 65% of innovation sales, saw 25% year-over-year growth, led by VitaBloom's average cost per velocity at $4.50 per case, with strong brick-and-mortar performance in the Sun Belt and 40% e-commerce share boosted by Amazon Prime Day. EMEA contributed 20% with 16% growth, where EarthCrunch gained UK traction via Tesco exclusives, taking 5% share in plant-based snacks despite 7% pricing pressure from Aldi private labels—our premium stance increased basket incidence. APAC at 10% exploded with 35% growth in China and India, as PureHarvest keto kits matched rising keto adoption up 40% per Kantar, with local Shanghai co-manufacturing trimming landed costs 12% amid U.S.-China tariffs. LATAM's 5% share grew 22% early on in Brazil and Mexico through VitaBloom's mango-ginger variant, using local sourcing against 10% inflation and FEMSA partnerships for C-store reach.

Looking ahead strategically, we're cementing TasteForge's innovation leadership against moves like PepsiCo's Poppi buy or Nestlé's vital proteins efforts. Our 12-month pipeline features seven SKUs, such as a mushroom-coffee ready-to-drink targeting the $2 billion nootropic market and granolas backed by regenerative agriculture. We're committing $150 million to R&D in FY24, emphasizing precision fermentation for dairy alternatives inspired by Perfect Day and AI flavor profiling to cut launch times from 18 to 12 months. Data from our 1.2 million LoyaltyClub members reveals 68% prioritize sustainability, guiding our net-zero packaging by 2030. We manage risks like 20% cocoa volatility with 60% hedged contracts and pea protein vertical integration. In short, innovations fueled superior growth and margins, fortifying our position; we anticipate 20-25% of FY24 revenue growth from them, backing our raised guidance of 8-10% organic sales and 12-14% EPS growth.

Second, concerning organic sales growth guidance for the next quarter and year. As we look ahead, our outlook for organic sales growth anchors our measured expansion strategy in the evolving Food & Beverage arena. For full fiscal 2024, we guide to 4.5% to 5.5% organic sales growth, exceeding our long-term 4% target and showcasing portfolio strength amid easing inflation and changing shopper habits. This projects Q3 organic growth of 3.5% to 4.5% and Q4 pickup to 5.0% to 6.0%, powered by seasonal snacking and beverage lifts, plus full-quarter pricing and innovation effects.

Breaking it down, organic growth balances pricing discipline at +3.0% to +3.5% annually—down from Q2's 4.2% as we lap tougher bases but holding via elasticities of 0.4 to 0.6, better than peers like Mondelez or Hershey facing cocoa pressures. Volumes eye flat to +0.5%, with at-home stabilization post-pantry stocking. Mix contributes +1.0% to +1.5% from premiumization, including 15% share gains in ready-to-drink coffee via TastyCore Nitro echoing Starbucks packaged wins, and double-digit plant-based snack growth under GreenBite.

By region, North America—55% of sales—leads at 5.0% to 6.0%, with savory chips up 7% in Q2 on household penetration, countering downtrading like at Kellogg or Campbell's, via affordable indulgence packs and premium ProFuel yogurt drinks targeting millennials à la Chobani. EMEA at 20% of sales guides 3.0% to 4.0%, with volume rebounds from new dairy in UK/Germany as out-of-home recovers post-Ukraine issues. Asia-Pacific, 15%, aims for 4.5% to 5.5%, driven by RedRush energy drinks up 12% year-over-year in China/India, watchful of FX and locals like Want Want. Latin America closes at 6.0% to 7.0%, leveraging beverage pricing power in Brazil/Mexico where soft drinks retain 40% loyalty despite health shifts; emerging markets fuel over 60% of incremental growth, mirroring Unilever and Nestlé trends.

This embeds key programs: a $250 million supply chain optimization with a new Texas aseptic line for ready-to-drink unlocking 2% volume by Q4 against 40% cocoa and 25% coffee spikes per Bloomberg. Precision pricing via AI tools like PepsiCo's rebate systems sustains 85% inflation pass-through. Innovation pace brings 12 SKUs in Q3/Q4, hitting the $50 billion better-for-you segment at 8% CAGR per NielsenIQ.

Trends support: snacking up 5% per IRI, premium ready-to-drink alcohols like Celsius' 25% surge, sustainability premiums with 70% recyclable snack packaging lifting loyalty 3 points. Headwinds like pricing fatigue, Frito-Lay promotions, commodity swings are met with 80% hedging through FY25. Overall, 4.5% to 5.5% positions us for top-quartile F&B results, with leverage to 12-13% EPS growth at midpoint, navigating health-value-indulgence blend.

Third, in terms of the impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions. These remain a major challenge across our packaged snacks, beverages, dairy, and plant-based lines like PureHarvest juices, CrunchTime snacks, and VitaDairy products, intensified by post-pandemic issues, geopolitics, weather extremes, and logistics strains. Quantitatively, input inflation lifted cost of goods sold 12% year-over-year in Q2 equivalent terms, causing 180 basis points of gross margin squeeze—from 42.1% last year to 40.3%—or 220 basis points underlying excluding prior insurance on crops. This equated to $145 million EBITDA hit, 7% below plan, aligning with Nestlé's 11% and PepsiCo's 13% North America reports.

By input, ag commodities at 55% of COGS led: wheat/corn up 22% from Black Sea limits and U.S. Midwest drought, hitting CrunchTime crackers/tortillas; vegetable oils 18% on El Niño palm floods; dairy 16% with U.S. milk powder 19% from avian flu herd cuts impacting VitaDairy; cocoa 35% to records from West Africa deficits like Hershey's hikes. Non-ag: aluminum 11% on energy, PET 9% on ethylene, diesel 15%, Asia-U.S. ocean rates 2.5x pre-pandemic via Red Sea.

Supply disruptions added 4-6 week lead variability and $28 million costs: L.A./Long Beach congestion at 10-day dwells delayed 15% APAC fruit purees; Europe trucking down 8% from strikes inflated EMEA freight 20%; Brazil trucker blocks caused 25% stockouts for bottling. On-time delivery fell to 88% from 95%, incurring $12 million slotting/expedites.

Regionally, North America (52% revenue) at 15.5% inflation from grains/dairy, offset pricing in snacks; EMEA (28%) 13% plus Ukraine grain ripples up 28% Euronext wheat for bakery; APAC/LATAM (20%) 11% with 30% volatility—Indonesia palm curbs, Brazil ethanol sugar diversion up 21%.

Our countermeasures: 9.2% revenue from pricing with -2.5 to -3.0 elasticities, mid-single hikes on 70% SKUs especially sticky plant-based. Hedging 65% ag at fixed—wheat $7.20/bushel vs. $9.50 spot, corn $5.80 vs. $7.20—saved $45 million YTD. Supplier shifts: Ukraine/Russia wheat to 8% from 18% via U.S./Australia, palm to Malaysian RSPO.

Digitally, AI demand sensing with SAP IBP/Refinitiv hit 92% forecast accuracy, cut safety stock 12%, saved $20 million writedowns. IBM Food Trust blockchain on 40% chain for alerts—rerouted 85% Red Sea shipments. Reformulations: 20% shea for cocoa butter, high-oleic sunflower for palm, saving 5-7% oils post-5,000 trials.

Forward, inflation eases to 7-9% H2 with USDA 5% corn rebound, Panama expansions; risks La Niña, farm bill. FY24 bakes 8-10% COGS inflation, margins 40-41% via $250 million Project Horizon zero-based procurement/manufacturing. This outpaces peers like Mondelez on cocoa via hedges/alts.

Fourth, looking at EPS guidance and key assumptions. Building on Q3 adjusted EPS of $1.42, up 12% year-over-year, we're raising full-year fiscal 2024 adjusted EPS to $5.85 to $6.00, implying 8-10% growth over 2023's $5.42, thanks to portfolio durability, NourishForward 2.0 productivity, and pricing in snacks, beverages, plant-based.

Key levers: Revenue organic +5% to +7% constant currency—4-5% pricing lapping softer prior, 2-3% FY25 hikes on premium functional beverages/protein snacks; 1-2% volume/mix from zero-sugar electrolytes like Gatorade G Zero, plant yogurt alts up 15% Nielsen Q3. North America (60%) +6-8% on salty share +2 points, convenience recovery; EMEA (20%) +4-6% pricing vs. dairy volatility, almond traction UK/Germany; APAC/LATAM (20%) +3-5% despite 3% FX drag (BRL/IDR), e-com China/India RTD teas +20%. U.S. CPI to 2.5-3%.

Gross margins +120-150 bps to 38.5% via NourishForward 2.0's $450 million savings ($150M ahead): 200 bps supply/AI forecasting waste -8% beverages, precision ag hedges 40% cocoa; 50 bps commodities 70% locked, dairy stable post-Ukraine, wheat -10%; 30 bps rPET pouches to 50% recycled 2025 like PepsiCo. No tariff jumps assumed.

SG&A flat to -20 bps at 22%: marketing 8% digital/ROI +25% CDP, G&A $80M zero-based, no big M&A but bolt-ons plant-based like Danone Alpro. Interest/tax: 23% ETR, $220M interest post-refi. FX 1-2% headwind ($0.05/10% USD). $1.2B repos 2% shares. CapEx $1.1B (3.5%) U.S. automation/APAC RTD coffee.

This pivots to healthspan—20% pipeline functional like collagen snacks, $100B+ 12% CAGR Euromonitor—ESG green bond $500M for 90% deforestation-free cocoa FY25. 45% staples buffer risks like inflation slowdown vs. discretionary peers.

Fifth, reviewing organic revenue growth overall and by region. Our organic revenue growth hit 5.2% year-over-year constant currency, stripping small Q1 organic yogurt acquisition and EMEA low-margin canned divestiture. This accelerates from Q2's 3.8% and Q1's 2.9%, tracking full-year 4.5-5.5%. It reflects core strength—snacks 42%, beverages 35%, dairy/plant-based 23%—against 6-8% global food inflation, Red Sea chains, softening sentiment.

Driven by 2.1% volumes, 2.8% pricing (ASP 3.2% exceeding on cocoa +25%/dairy +12% pass-through), 0.3% mix to premiums. Regions balanced:

North America (57% revenue) 4.8%—volumes +1.7% on Harvest Bites protein bars +12% share +110 bps Nielsen, +2,500 Walmart/Kroger doors, e-com 8% NA (Amazon/D2C +25%). Pricing +2.9% lapping promos vs. syrups; mix flat, soft drinks -1% offset VitaQuench +8% wellness (IRI +4% non-alc). $50M Ohio fermentation saves 20% plant dairy +15% vs. privates.

EMEA (22%) strongest 6.5% from Q2 4.2%, volumes +3.4% summer iced tea/snacks +5% UK/Germany, +1,200 Tesco/Rewe EcoCrunch recyclable EU PPWR. Pricing +2.6% vs. dairy deflation, mix +0.5% organic yogurts +18% 25% ASP premium Chobani-style. Middle East +9% Gulf snacks $10B 7% CAGR; Turkey inflation hedged 30% local nuts. €40M ERP to 8.2x turns +10% replenishment.

Asia-Pacific (14%) 7.2%, volumes +4.1% China post-COVID snacks +11% matcha beverages +80 bps vs. Want Want ($120M China +15%); pricing +2.4%, mix +0.7% ZenFlow kombucha +22% 12% CAGR Kantar. India +13% dairy kiranas/UPI; palm reformulation -8% costs Indonesia +6%. $30M Vietnam hub Q4 20% savings 10%+ CAGR.

Latin America (7%) 3.1% vs. Argentina 140%/Brazil FX—volumes +0.8% TropiMix +9% Mexico vs. Bimbo EDLP; pricing +3.8% wheat/sugar absorbed 2% efficiencies; mix -0.1% bev soft offset plant milks +14% 15% vegan growth. $15M agritech cacao traceability vs. El Niño.

Ahead, Q4 5-6% holiday/new RTD coffee 5 SKUs, $200M capex automation/cold-chain vs. 2.5% spoilage. Risks cocoa $5K, recession; 45% margins +120 bps buffer AI 92% forecast. Targeting 5%+ via health 30% portfolio 2025, net-zero Scope 1/2 2030, e-com 12% +5 points—outpacing Mondelez 3.9%/PepsiCo 4.3% on volumes.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Michael Chen (CFO):
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3 2023. Net sales were $2.85 billion, representing a 9% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 42.5%, impacted by input cost inflation partially offset by productivity gains and mix from innovations. Operating income was $485 million, and earnings per share were $1.42. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $1.5 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for 8-10% organic sales growth and 12-14% EPS growth.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, thank you. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your business?

Sarah Thompson (CEO):
Thanks, John. As I detailed earlier, input cost inflation rose about 12% year-over-year on COGS, compressing margins 180 basis points, with ag commodities like cocoa up 35% and dairy 16% leading the charge. Supply disruptions added variability, but our hedging at 65%, pricing pass-through at 9.2%, and reformulations have stabilized us ahead of peers, with margins holding firm at 42.5% thanks to productivity.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Emily Chen (JPMorgan):
What are your plans for new product and what is the expected impact of product?

Lisa Patel (Chief Growth Officer):
Good question, Emily. Our pipeline is robust with seven SKUs over 12 months, including mushroom-coffee RTDs and regenerative granolas, backed by $150 million R&D. Building on Q3's $285 million incremental from VitaBloom, EarthCrunch, and PureHarvest—which drove 22% top-line—we expect 20-25% of FY24 growth from innovations, with superior 50%+ margins and trends in health, sustainability, and convenience fueling outsized returns.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with Barclays. Please proceed.

Mike Rodriguez (Barclays):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

David Ruiz (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Mike, we've tackled this head-on with AI demand sensing boosting forecast accuracy to 92%, blockchain for 40% traceability enabling preemptive Red Sea reroutes, and supplier diversification cutting Ukraine wheat reliance to 8%. On-time delivery is rebounding to 90%+, with new capacity like Texas aseptic lines mitigating port delays and strikes—saving $20 million in inventory while supporting 9.2x turns on innovations.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Sarah Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Sarah Lee (Morgan Stanley):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Michael Chen (CFO):
Sarah, our raised FY24 EPS guide of $5.85-$6.00 assumes 5-7% organic revenue, 120-150 bps margin expansion via NourishForward savings, and flat SG&A—bolstered by Q4 acceleration to 5-6% organic on seasons and launches. Risks like FX or commodities are hedged, positioning 8-10% organic sales and strong leverage.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in TasteForge Inc. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
